pr_title: Add a --lint flag to the promtool check rules and check config commands
pr_body:
Checking rules with promtool emits warnings in the case of duplicate rules.
These warnings do not result in a non-zero exit code and are difficult to
spot in CI environments. Additionally, checking for duplicates is closer
to a lint check rather than a syntax check.

This commit adds a --lint flag to commands which include checking rules.
The flag can be used to enable or disable certain linting options
and cause the execution to return a non-zero exit code in case
those options are not met.

Fixes #8613

Signed-off-by: fpetkovski <filip.petkovsky@gmail.com>

pr_comments: Thanks for the review. Would you like me to do the rebase on this branch, or would that happen automatically when merging to main?

Hi. Just a quick question here; running v2.35 of promtool now exits for us with code 3 as we have duplicate rule names defined - which makes sense from the changes here. However Prometheus v2.35 still starts with duplicate rules - is this correct, or should Prometheus also reject duplicate rules?
Yes, I believe that is expected behavior. Duplicate rules are completely fine, they're just something that's rarely actually intended, hence it being a lint check.

Hello!
Regarding @mogoman question: We have the same problem. We had to disable the linting option "duplicate-rules" as it fails since this lint option is included in the promtool.

@LeviHarrison you already wrote, that it's completely fine as it's intended like this to have "duplicate" rules. But will this be deprecated (and unsupported) in the future, so that we have to fix this issue?

Is there anywhere a documentation with best practices how alerting rules should be defined incl. such information how you can avoid "duplicate rules"? We for example have multiple alerts with the same alert rule name, but with different thresholds, severities and sometimes even `for`. The reason for it is, that we wanted to overwrite active alerts with a low severity with a higher severity.

Thank you in advance!

Hi @Sebi94nbg -- for the current problem please upgrade promtool to at least 2.36.1, we've fixed the error status in that release.

I'm afraid there aren't very good docs on this -- we have #7301 open to track some improvements. With alert rules usually this is dealt with by having different labels identifying the alerts; something like:

```yaml
groups:
  - name: example
    rules:
      - alert: JobDown
        expr: my_warning_query
        labels:
          severity: warning
      - alert: JobDown
        expr: my_critical_query
        labels:
          severity: critical
```

The issue being alerts are identified by the complete set of labels, so if two alerts have exactly the same labels it is possible for strange things to happen (you mention `for` and that is one potential place where duplicated rules can cause alerts to resolve when one rule is still firing, etc). However in many cases this isn't a problem as labels flow through from the metrics (which the lint currently doesn't take into account).

Duplicate rules are a fine use case. Not sure how to deal with them yet.

issue_context.title: promtool: Support some kind of “lint” for rules
issue_context.body:
`promtool check rules` currently is [documented](https://prometheus.io/docs/prometheus/latest/configuration/recording_rules/#syntax-checking-rules) as a way to syntax check rules. However it also checks for duplicate rules, which is closer to a lint check.

There are some features in PromQL that are potentially problematic to use in recording rules now:
- Negative offset is likely incorrect in recording rules (I mentioned some kind of lint [then](https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/issues/6282#issuecomment-550308545))
- Subqueries are often not a good idea (noted on the [blog post](https://prometheus.io/blog/2019/01/28/subquery-support/))

I propose something like a `--lint` flag where the default is “duplicate-rules” to match current behaviour, but could also accept `--lint=all`, etc. 

(Some overlap with #8607)
comments: This was planned as part of #7779 but that's inactive at the moment for the reviewing process. If we can resume work there, then I can extend the pretty process as described here.
This sounds like a good idea.
Another lint that came up is checking for an annotation: label in alerting rules: #8864.
